Ghana’s PFM legal framework, ordered from higher to lower legal authority, is:

1. Constitution of the Republic of Ghana, 1992 — constitutional tier.
2. Public Financial Management Act, 2016 (Act 921) — Act of Parliament.
3. Public Procurement Act, 2003 (Act 663), as amended — Act of Parliament.
4. Internal Audit Agency Act, 2003 (Act 658) — Act of Parliament.
5. Public Financial Management Regulations, 2019 (L.I. 2378) — implementing regulations under the PFM Act.

Acts of Parliament are at the statutory tier below the Constitution. Legislative Instruments and other regulations are lower-tier instruments implementing statutory provisions. Ministerial guidelines, such as the PFM Commitment Control Guidelines, are administrative guidance rather than laws or regulations; the Ministry states that applicable PFM laws prevail where a guideline conflicts with them.
